title: Checking a solution by substitution
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:19Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches checking a solution by substitution: one solves quadratics by reading x-intercepts from a graph at Year 9 depth, and the other solves simultaneous equations by substitution at Year 10 depth, so no existing point matches this Stage 4 idea.

draft.title: Checking a solution by substitution
card: To check a solution, put it back into the original equation in place of the letter. Work out the left side and the right side separately.
If both sides are equal, the solution is right. If they are not equal, the solution is wrong and you need to solve again.
Always use the original equation, not your working. Then a mistake made earlier cannot hide.
Is \(x = 6\) a solution of \(3x - 5 = 13\)? Left side: \(3 \times 6 - 5 = 18 - 5 = 13\). Right side: \(13\). Both sides are equal, so \(x = 6\) is correct.
draft.remember: A solution is right only when both sides of the original equation come out equal.

a.q: Which value of \(x\) is a solution of \(2x + 4 = 18\)?
a.why: Put \(x = 7\) in: \(2 \times 7 + 4 = 14 + 4 = 18\), which equals the right side. For \(x = 11\), the left side is \(26\), not \(18\). That value comes from adding 4 to 7 by mistake instead of checking.
a.clue: Put each value in and see if the left side equals 18.

b.q: Mia solved \(5x - 3 = 22\) and got \(x = 4\). She checks it. What does she find?
opts: The left side is 17, so her answer is wrong
Both sides are 22, so her answer is right
The left side is 17, so her answer is right
The left side is 20, so her answer is wrong
b.why: Put \(x = 4\) in: \(5 \times 4 - 3 = 20 - 3 = 17\). The right side is \(22\), so the sides are not equal and the answer is wrong. The correct solution is \(x = 5\).
b.clue: Work out \(5 \times 4 - 3\) and compare it with 22.

b.best: The left side is 17, so her answer is wrong
